item.title: Citadel's Esposito on Bank Partnerships, Fixed Income Growth
item.description: Citadel Securities President Jim Esposito discusses the firm's relationship with banks, plans to grow in the fixed income market and his views on prediction markets with Bloomberg's Dani Burger on the sidelines of Citadel's annual Future of Global Markets Conference in New York. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Citadel Looking to Grow in Fixed Income, Esposito Says
item.description: "We're only really getting started in fixed income," Citadel Securities President Jim Esposito says during an interview with Bloomberg's Dani Burger on the sidelines of Citadel's annual Future of Global Markets Conference in New York. Esposito also says the firm is "maniacally" focused on market making. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jeanne Sun Favors US Stocks as AI Rally Continues
item.description: Jeanne Sun of Citi discusses resilient earnings, AI-driven productivity gains and how investors are navigating market volatility. She says Citi favors US equities while remaining cautious on Treasuries as strong growth and sticky inflation pressure yields. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Fears Roar Back, Tech Earnings on Deck
item.description:
A rebound in the artificial intelligence trade sputtered after the dismal debut of a South Korean data center firm revived concerns about whether the technology’s spending boom can last.
Seoul’s Kospi Index fell 3.8% on a fresh bout of weakness in two of the world’s biggest memory makers, Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. AI infrastructure group Elice Inc. suffered the worst opening day for a sizable company on the bourse, even after an initial public offering that was 400 times subscribed.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Anna Edwards, Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Halts Poultry Shipments to China After Disease Outbreak
item.description: Brazil has halted all poultry shipments to its biggest buyer China after confirming a case of viral, highly contagious Newcastle disease.
item.dc:creator: Dayanne Sousa and Ana Mano

item.title: Brazil Traders Ramp Up Hedges Ahead of Tight Election Runoff
item.description: Investors are ramping up hedges ahead of Brazil’s presidential runoff as polls point to a tight race between right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro and the incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.
item.dc:creator: Barbara Nascimento and David Marino

item.title: Elice Plunges in Trading Debut; General Motors Falls on Forecast | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Elice (KS) is floundering as it plunged in their trading debut, falling as much as 38% and finishing the day with a 32% loss. The selloff threatened a tentative recovery in Asian stocks and revived concerns over neoclouds, as rising borrowing costs and doubts over returns from massive AI spending sour investor appetite. - GE Aerospace (GE) is moving after raising its full-year outlook amid strong aircraft engine demand, despite resurgent jet fuel prices. - General Motors (GM) shares are lower after the company narrowed its full-year profit forecast and will buy back another $20 billion in stock, reflecting strong cash flows. General Motors reported higher profit and revenue in the latest quarter despite selling fewer cars. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Centerbridge, Mubadala in Talks to Buy Canaccord’s UK Wealth Unit
item.description: Canaccord Genuity Group Inc. is in talks to sell its UK wealth management business to a consortium led by private equity firm Centerbridge Partners, according to people with knowledge of the matter.
item.dc:creator: Crystal Tse and Swetha Gopinath

item.title: ¿Por qué el frenesí de deuda por la IA inquieta a los mercados?
item.description: Las grandes tecnológicas están gastando miles de millones para competir en IA y los inversionistas empiezan a buscar protección frente a su deuda. La preocupación está en cuánto costará esta carrera y si generará suficientes ingresos y retornos para justificar el endeudamiento (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Top-Rated Junk Debt Becomes Sweet Spot as Investors Flee Risk
item.description: High-grade investors, including T. Rowe Price Associates Inc. and Invesco, are looking at dipping into the least risky corner of junk debt after a broader selloff pushed valuations lower.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Tayeb

item.title: Bessent Sees No Spillover From France Bond Market’s Turmoil
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he doesn’t anticipate a spillover from the French bond market, which has seen surging yields that have in turn driven a broader conversation about the European nation’s finances.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: S&P 500 Rebounds as Big Bank Stocks Climb, SpaceX Results Loom
item.description: The S&P 500 Index rose, erasing its early-session losses, as big banks and healthcare companies climbed. The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 Index rebounded to a slight gain after South Korean neocloud company Elice Inc. tanked in its trading debut, spurring concern about the sustainability of the global AI boom that continued to weigh on the sector.
item.dc:creator: Felice Maranz

item.title: AI Fears Return With Data Center IPO Flop; SpaceX, Netflix Earnings
item.description: US equity futures slip, pausing an AI recovery in stocks, after South Korean data center company Elice plunged in its trading debut. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy heads to Norway for fresh peace talks as tensions with the US deepens. SpaceX, Netflix, General Motors, RTX, and Northrop are set to report earnings. Jeanne Sun of Citigroup Global Markets joins "Bloomberg Brief" to discuss her outlook for this earnings season. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Halliburton Sees Lasting Growth as Mideast Rebuilds From War
item.description: Halliburton Co. is predicting years of growth for oil field service work as nations replenish crude reserves and the Middle East rebuilds infrastructure damaged in the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Emma Sanchez

item.title: European Gas Prices Slump After Climbing to Four-Year Highs
item.description: European natural gas retreated sharply after hitting €90 for the first time in almost four years, with some traders taking profits from the recent rally.
item.dc:creator: Elena Mazneva and Priscila Azevedo Rocha

item.title: Senegal Bonds Plunge as Budget Standoff Puts IMF Deal at Risk
item.description: Senegal’s dollar bonds suffered their biggest drop since early September after opposition leader Ousmane Sonko threatened to block a revised 2026 budget and the government’s spending plan for next year.
item.dc:creator: Katarina Höije and Ray Ndlovu

item.title: Netflix Needs Blockbusters to Reverse Its $135 Billion Wipeout
item.description: Netflix Inc. needs to prove that it can produce hit movies and TV series again to stop a slide that has erased more than $135 billion in market value this year.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Reinicke

item.title: Stocks Rise as US-Iran Hopes Trigger Oil Decline: Markets Wrap
item.description: Wall Street traders drove stocks and bonds higher as oil prices dropped on hopes for a diplomatic way to the end the war in Iran.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Oct. 20
item.description: Brent oil fell on an unconfirmed report that Qatar and Pakistan had issued a fresh proposal to revive negotiations to bring an end to the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Mia Gindis

item.title: CIBC Sells C$1 Billion Limited Recourse Capital Notes
item.description: Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce sold C$1 billion ($710 million) of additional tier-one bonds on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Chunzi Xu
